At the top of its stroke, the piston seals off the upper chamber, trapping pressurized water. When the water level in the lower chamber drops, gravity pulls the piston back down, creating a vacuum that sucks more water into the lower chamber. This process repeats itself, with each stroke delivering water to a higher elevation than the previous one.
